articles.title: PIXEL 11 PRO FOLD DESIGN LEAKS AHEAD OF GOOGLE LAUNCH EVENT
articles.summary: Leaked marketing renders from Evan Blass reportedly reveal the unannounced Pixel 11 Pro Fold, alongside new Pixel Buds and a Pixel Watch, ahead of Google's launch event. The foldable appears similar to last year's model, keeping a tall outer screen and 8-inch inner display, but with a redesigned camera array featuring a glowy light teased for the Pixel 11 Pro. Google's Made by Google event is set for August 12th, where these devices are expected to be announced, though prices may rise.

articles.title: A PROPERTIES PANEL AND ANNOTATIONS, NOW IN FIGMA MAKE
articles.summary: Figma Make now includes a properties panel and annotations, letting users edit designs visually or with in-context prompts instead of relying solely on text. The properties panel adjusts spacing, typography, and layout directly, while annotations let users mark elements and describe changes like hover effects or animations for the agent to apply. Both features roll out to all seats and plans, consume credits, and currently only work with new Make designs, not previously created ones.

articles.title: REDDIT IS TESTING A NEW WAY TO WATCH AND LISTEN TO ITS VIRAL POSTS
articles.summary: Reddit is testing a new TikTok-inspired video experience that would let users watch videos based on viral Reddit posts and listen to narrated stories in the background. CEO Steve Huffman said the company is responding to the popularity of Reddit-story content on platforms like TikTok, where millions of videos already repurpose Reddit discussions with text-to-speech narration. The feature is expected to enter testing later this year, as Reddit continues expanding its video offerings following the recent launch of video comments.

articles.title: JAKOB'S LAW: HOW TO APPLY IT AS AI COLLAPSES SURFACES INTO ONE CHAT BOX
articles.summary: Jakob's Law still applies in the AI era, but the reference point has shifted from websites to AI assistants like ChatGPT, Claude, and Copilot. As users increasingly start tasks through conversational interfaces rather than individual apps, products need to be discoverable, understandable, and usable through assistants by using clear naming, structured data, standard UI patterns, and protocols like MCP and A2UI. Rather than designing only for users who visit an app directly, designers should also optimize for products that work behind the scenes, with AI assistants becoming the primary interface for many tasks.

articles.title: YOUR PEOPLE GET AI. GET OUT OF THEIR WAY
articles.summary: Despite widespread investment in AI, 95% of corporate AI projects fail, not because of the technology but because bureaucracy, excessive approvals, and a lack of trust prevent capable employees from using it effectively. Smaller, empowered teams can make fast decisions and focus on solving real problems, while large organizations often reward control over judgment, creating "organizational debt" that slows innovation. The companies that will benefit most from AI won't be those with the best tools - they'll be the ones that trust their people, remove unnecessary layers of management, and let experienced employees openly experiment, share what works, and make decisions.

articles.title: HOW TO REDUCE AI DRIFTING IN DESIGN
articles.summary: Design systems drift when Figma components and front-end code fall out of sync, and AI often widens that gap rather than closing it. A proposed fix uses "component contracts" — plain-language specs that become the shared source of truth — paired with harness engineering, deterministic guardrails surrounding an AI model. Testing showed an AI agent scored 100/100 building screens from a contract catalog, versus 69/100 when ungoverned.

articles.title: FOR 100 YEARS NO ONE NOTICED IT, BUT THIS REBRAND FINALLY GIVES GUNNERSBURY MUSEUM A REASON TO BE FOUND
articles.summary: Gunnersbury Museum and Park has introduced a new modular identity by Wiedemann Lampe to solve a long-standing visibility problem: most people knew the park but not the museum. The system uses separate symbols and colors—a green tree for the park and a purple building for the museum—that combine into a yellow identity when representing both together, giving each its own voice while maintaining a cohesive brand. Supported by flexible illustrations, human-focused photography, and intuitive yellow wayfinding, the rebrand is designed to increase awareness, encourage exploration, and help the historic site become a more recognizable cultural destination.

articles.title: BETHESDA'S NEW LOGO DESIGN BRINGS PEAK GAMING NOSTALGIA WITH A NOD TO ITS ICONIC ORIGINAL BRANDING
articles.summary: To celebrate its 40th anniversary, Bethesda has introduced a new retro-futuristic logo that replaces its clean, corporate identity with one inspired by the company's original 1980s and 1990s branding. The redesign brings back the "Bethesda Softworks" name, uses an angular cyberpunk-inspired typeface reminiscent of its early years, and aims to better reflect the publisher's long history and personality. Fans have overwhelmingly praised the change, seeing it as a welcome return to Bethesda's roots and a reminder that distinctive branding can be more memorable than generic minimalism.

articles.title: GOOGLE'S SYNTHID WATERMARK IS HARD TO BREAK, BUT IT DOESN'T SOLVE AI DISINFORMATION
articles.summary: Google's SynthID watermark survived 300 rounds of simulated compression and resizing in testing, though cropping combined with heavy compression eventually defeated it. Even so, watermarking can't solve AI disinformation broadly, since fragmented detection systems, usage limits, and unlabeled open-source models leave huge gaps. Experts argue the better long-term strategy is authenticating genuine content via cryptographic metadata like C2PA rather than trying to flag every piece of synthetic media.

articles.title: THE AI AESTHETIC
articles.summary: AI has spawned distinct design idioms—sparkle emojis, streaming text, shimmering "thinking" indicators, tiny icons, and beige/cream palettes with orange accents—some likely to fade, others already spreading into broader software design.
